Description:



What is the 2 Mukhi Rudraksha?


The 2 Mukhi Rudraksha is a sacred bead with two natural lines or faces on its surface. It is also known as the Do Mukhi or Two-Faced Rudraksha. It symbolizes the unified companionship of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati, who are also known as Ardhanarishwara, the half-male and half-female form of the Supreme Lord. The 2 Mukhi Rudraksha represent the duality of creation and the balance of opposites.


It is also the manifestation of the Moon, the ruling planet of this Rudraksha, and this planet influences the emotions, mind, and imagination. Wearing this bead helps diminish the negative effects of the moon, such as mood swings, depression, and lack of concentration. It also balances the material and spiritual aspects of human life, as well as the masculine and feminine energies within oneself.  Our 2 Mukhi Rudraksha is available in collector, super collector, & Haridwar sizes.



About the ruling planet moon

The ruling planet of 2 Mukhi Rudraksha is Chandra, considered the representation of the mind and emotions. The Moon is the source of light at night and influences the tides, seasons, and cycles of life. It is associated with intuition, imagination, creativity, and sensitivity. The 2 Mukhi Rudraksha helps balance and harmonize the effects of the moon in one’s horoscope. It can help overcome the challenges and obstacles that the Moon may bring, such as mood swings, depression, anxiety, and insecurity. It can also help enhance the positive qualities of the moon, such as love, compassion, empathy, and joy.


Different ways to wear the 2 Mukhi Rudraksha

The 2 Mukhi Rudraksha is a versatile piece of accessory. Some of the common ways to wear it are:

  • The 2 Mukhi Rudraksha can be worn as a single bead or in combination with other Mukhi rudraksha. It can be strung in a silk/wool thread or capped in silver or gold. It can be worn on either hand like a bracelet or around the neck.
  • The 2 Mukhi Rudraksha can be worn in popular combinations like the Siddha Mala, the Indra Mala, or the Maha Mrityunjay Mala.
  • However, before wearing any of these ways, one should follow some guidelines and precautions, such as:
  • Buying them from a trusted seller who can provide a certificate of authenticity and lab testing report
  • Checking their shape and origin
  • Consulting an astrologer or our expert recommenders to choose a suitable one.
  • Wearing them on a Monday morning after taking a bath and wearing clean clothes
  • Keeping them clean and dry


Story about the presiding deity:

As per ancient texts, there was a demon named Adi who could change his form at will. To entice Lord Shiva he approached him under the guise of Devi Parvati. Lord Shiva, the all-seeing God recognized this deceit and killed him. However, Goddess Parvati was furious to see another woman with Lord Shiva. She cursed Nandi, his gatekeeper to turn into a stone idol.

Parvati’s fury knew no bounds. Lord Brahma decided to intervene and took away her dark, furious form (Kali). Parvati then took on a poised golden form called Gauri. Lord Brahma then blessed her and claimed her form would merge with her husband’s form so closely that nobody would ever separate both of her. This is how the Ardhanareeshwar form was first eulogized.

What is the Gaurishankar Rudraksha?


The Gaurishankar Rudraksha is a special bead that consists of two naturally joined Rudrakshas, symbolizing the union and companionship of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. This Rudraksha brings harmony, happiness, and prosperity in relationships, especially marriage. The ruling planet of the Gaurishankar Rudraksha is the Moon, the planet of emotions, mind, and creativity. The ruling deity of the Gaurishankar Rudraksha is Shiv Shakti, the divine couple that represents the balance of masculine and feminine energies. Wearing this Rudraksha attracts the grace of both, Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati, making it a promising choice for anyone seeking to enhance their love and devotion. The Gaurishankar Rudraksha is available in large and collector sizes.


Different ways to wear the Gaurishankar Rudraksha


The Gaurishankar Rudraksha can be worn in different ways depending on one’s preference and purpose. Some of the common ways are:

  • The Gaurishankar Rudraksha can be worn as a single bead or in combination with other Mukhi Rudraksha. It can be strung in a silk/wool thread or capped in silver or gold. It can be worn on either hand or around the neck.
  • The Gaurishankar Rudraksha can be worn in our popular combinations like the Gaurishankar Kantha, Indra Mala, Siddha mala, or the Maha Mrityunjay mala. 
  • A personalized combination can be made by using the free recommendation of our experts to know which combination will provide you with the best outcomes.
  • However, before wearing any of these ways, one should follow some guidelines and precautions, such as:
  • Buying them from a trusted seller who can provide a certificate of authenticity and lab testing report checking their shape and origin
  • Consulting an astrologer
  • Wearing them the next morning after taking a bath and wearing clean clothes
  • Keeping them clean and dry



Story about the presiding deity:


Shiva and Shakti were the supreme couple of the universe, but they had different interests and personalities. Shakti, as Parvati, tried to win Shiva’s love by serving him, but he ignored her. She then performed a severe penance, which impressed Shiva, but he tested her faith by sending a messenger to discourage her. Parvati remained loyal and devoted, and Shiva revealed himself and asked her to marry him. They celebrated their wedding and became one in body, mind, and soul. Story about the presiding deity:


Lord Ganesha was the son of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati, and the god of wisdom, success, and good luck. He had an elephant head, a big belly, and four arms, and he rode on a mouse. He was very fond of sweets, especially sweets. He was invited to a feast by Kubera, the god of wealth, who wanted to show off his riches. Ganesha ate all the food that Kubera had and asked for more. He threatened to eat Kubera and his palace if he did not get more food. Kubera prayed to Lord Shiva, who came to his rescue. He scolded Ganesha for his greed and gluttony and cursed him that he would become fat and have a big belly. He also blessed him with wisdom and success and made him the remover of obstacles, and the first to be worshipped before any auspicious occasion. He made his belly a symbol of prosperity and happiness, and his mouse a symbol of humility and service. He made him the most beloved and revered god of all, and the god of Ganesha, the supreme being.

product_data.wearingRules:
How to Care for Your Siddha Mala


  • Clean the mala once a month with a soft brush and apply a little almond oil.


  • Before wearing it again, chant “Om Namah Shivaya” 11 times.


  • Remove it before attending a funeral or during intimate relations.


  • If consuming alcohol or non-vegetarian food, you may remove it and wear it again afterwards.


  • Women can wear the Siddha Mala during all phases of life, including menstruation.


  • For regular energization, touch it to a Shivling and chant Om Namah Shivaya 11 times.


A Rudrabhishek offers additional spiritual energization.


  • Do not wear a Rudraksha that has already been worn by someone else.


  • Keep separate malas for daily wear and mantra chanting (Japa).


  • Avoid immersing the Mala in heavy liquids such as Ghee or Honey as they may enter the crevices of the bead and make it difficult to wear.
